newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon lodges complaint against Israel.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon lodges complaint against Israel.

text.p: The Lebanese government on Wednesday filed a complaint with a five-nation committee monitoring a ceasefire understanding in south Lebanon over an Israeli air raid that wounded a civilian.
Beirut's official National News Agency said Lebanon lodged a complaint over the wounding of a shepherd in Tuesday's air attack on pro-Iranian Hizbollah targets near the eastern town of Baalbek.

The shepherd was hit by debris from exploding rockets which destroyed the transmission antenna of Hizbollah's radio station, security sources have said. Israeli jets also targeted bases of a radical Palestinian group on Tuesday.
The ceasefire committee was set up to monitor a U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon last April in which some 200 people, mostly civilians, were killed.

The agreement bars both Israel and Hizbollah (Party of God) from targeting civilian areas but allows guerrilla attacks on Israeli forces occupying a border zone in south Lebanon and gives both sides the right to self-defence.

The agency said the ceasefire monitors -- delegates of the United States, France, Lebanon, Syria and Israel -- would meet next Monday to discuss the Lebanese complaint and another complaint filed by Israel against Beirut.
Israel filed the complaint last Friday, saying its forces found five bombs planted by a road near the village of Beit Lif in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, the agency said.
The ceasefire monitors meet at the coastal headquarters of the UNIFIL peacekeepers in the south Lebanon zone.
